name: inprocess-obi-tlul-timer-f5
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches one real OpenTitan TL-UL rv_timer in one process and takes its real level interrupt: the F5 firmware writes the declared timer trigger sequence, the CPU's machine-external input receives the RTL's intr_timer_expired_hart0_timer0_o, the ISR reads INTR_STATE0 at 0x104 and stores it, and the declared compare re-arm clears the state inside the same RTL. F2 and F4 exercise the same TL-UL target in the same session.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches one TL-UL target at 0x40004000 behind the real beat_to_tlul adapter; the profile's own protocol is tl-ul/1 (address_width 32, data_width 32, integrity required, one outstanding), so no APB3 target is in this build.

The behavior file configs/behaviors/opentitan_rv_timer_f5.json is the declaration this increment adds. It names the RTL's own interrupt output intr_timer_expired_hart0_timer0_o (rv_timer.sv:31,77), the INTR_STATE0 status word at 0x104, cause bit 0, the trigger sequence CTRL(0x4)=1, COMPARE_LOWER0_0(0x118)=0, COMPARE_UPPER0_0(0x11c)=0 (its reset value is 0xffffffff, so the upper word must be written too), INTR_ENABLE0(0x100)=1, and the clear COMPARE_LOWER0_0(0x118)=0xffffff00.

The clear is the RTL's compare-update clear (rv_timer.sv:82-83): mtimecmp_update deasserts intr_state0. A W1C write to INTR_STATE0 cannot keep the level low while the timer is still enabled and mtime >= mtimecmp, because prim_intr_hw re-sets the event every tick; re-arming the compare makes mtime < mtimecmp and the raw output really falls. The ISR still reads INTR_STATE0 before the clear.

Window: the profile's own 4 KiB rv_timer window at 0x40004000..0x40005000. The pinned F2/F4 scenario uses 0x40003000; this scenario moves the window only to keep room for an optional DMA control window at 0x40003000 without an overlap. 0x40004000..0x40005000 clears the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000 and the 4 GiB bound.

No DMA is declared, so F6 is refused as unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:TL-UL. F1-F5 are runnable: the CPU exports IRQ and RVFI retirement, the TL-UL target declares the four F5 facts, and the target's real output is wired to the CPU's declared external input.

A second target with a different protocol is not declared: target_protocol_axis refuses a TL-UL + APB3 session as unsupported-targets:mixed-protocol:apb3,tl-ul. The APB3 timer/I2C combinations keep their own scenarios and evidence.
This file declares the scenario; it is not evidence. The real run under runs/p0-1-ip/ is the evidence, and it claims only what its case lines read from the device.
